author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: ASM / Advanced WAF: give the application security logging profile a remote storage destination (the data collector) in the Key-Value Pairs (Splunk) or Common Event Format (ArcSight) format. Requests with no violation go to HTTP (logged only when the profile's request type is all requests); violations, blocked or alerted requests and attack events (brute force, web scraping, DoS) go to NIDS. The comma separated format is positional and isn't covered. Times have no zone and are read as UTC. APM: send access logs to the data collector over remote syslog (RFC 3164). New session, username, policy ending, access policy result, AD authentication failure and session deleted messages go to Auth, each with the session ID; APM splits one logon over several lines, so join them on session_id in search. F5 publishes no full APM message catalogue, so only these confirmed messages are read. In a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 the engine rejoined a quoted key=value value that holds a comma with a space, so the ASM parent reads those fields with their own patterns. The tenant's built-in F5_LTM parser also matches the APM lines and normalizes nothing; the engine picks one parser per line, and the APM parser took them in 7 of 10 Run Tests. No built-in parser matched the ASM lines. Samples are made up from F5's examples and field lists. Each ASM child, combined with the parent into one parser, and the APM parser passed Run Test there, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines. On 2026-10-14 each ASM child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under the parent.
